name: Horrid Creations

source.reason: Explicit CUR-003 source reference; edition/permission not certified.

originalText:
Horrid Creations
A great many creatures, foul and monstrous, owe their
existence to the trolls, who made armies of monsters
by sculpting the flesh of ordinary things and seeding
unthinking hatred within them. From lumbering giants to
two-headed ogres, a whole menagerie of ugly, slimy, toothy,
and violent beasts slipped into the world from cauldrons of
filth. The Men of Gog, having plundered the emptied troll
cities in the Desolation, discovered these same techniques
and used them to breed their own horrors. If one adds to
them the horde of undead let loose upon the world, and
demons bound in particular forms and functions, the Men
of Gog did more to disrupt the natural order of things than
anyone before or after.

name: Abominations

source.reason: Explicit CUR-003 source reference; edition/permission not certified.

originalText:
Abominations
The Witch-King rarely summarily executed those subjects
who were close to him. Doing so would simply send them
to Hell or the Underworld, and the loss of their knowledge
and experience might diminish all of his people. However,
Ashrakal showed great creativity when it came to punishing
those who disappointed him. Most of his brides he
“granted” eternal life as gorgons as a way of punishing their
vanity. These accursed women haunt old, desolate places
where they nurse their ancient hatred. Other subjects he
warped into lamias (see Tombs of the Desolation), who still
live in caves and ruins across the Desolation, luring victims
into their lairs to make them their eternal slaves.
